fun_facts: A hooked jack crevalle fights so hard for so long that the exertion alone can be nearly lethal: anglers who want it to survive release often have to revive it boatside for several minutes before it can swim off under its own power.

Jack crevalle hunt in coordinated packs, driving schools of baitfish into a tight ball and sometimes pushing them right up onto a sloping beach, a hunting style closer to how dolphins corral fish than how most inshore fish feed.
A jack crevalle's heart and gills are oversized for a fish its size, built for the kind of sustained, high-speed chase that leaves most other inshore species behind after the first burst.
